events.name: Scott Silven
events.info: The Lost Things is a journey through wonder, memory, and the strange beauty hidden inside the things we lose. Created and performed by celebrated illusionist Scott Silven and directed by Graham McLaren, the show weaves awe-inspiring illusions together with a deeply personal narrative to create something that feels less like a magic show and more like a profound shared experience. Silven believes theatre is where we gather to witness the impossible together, and The Lost Things is built entirely around that belief. Designed by Jamie Vartan and featuring illusions that have left audiences genuinely speechless, The Lost Things has earned a reputation as one of the most moving and inventive shows of its kind. Arizona Arts Live is a proud co-commissioner of this production, making Tucson part of the story of this remarkable work. This is an evening that will make you look at memory, loss, and the surprising places where wonder lives differently. Recommended for ages 12 and up. Experience

Dancing in the Streets AZ presents - The Nutcracker Ballet
events.info: This holiday season, discover the magic of The Nutcracker Ballet for Everybody! Join Dancing In The Streets AZ as we bring Tucsons beloved holiday tradition to life with breathtaking dancing, dazzling costumes, enchanting storytelling, and live music by the Polar Bear Orchestra, featuring the Snow Flake Chorus. Follow Clara on her unforgettable journey through the sparkling Land of Snow and the magical Kingdom of Sweets in a production that celebrates the joy, beauty, and wonder of the holiday season. At Dancing In The Streets AZ, we believe Ballet for Everybody means everyone belongs. Our inspiring cast reflects our community-bringing together dancers of all ages, backgrounds, abilities, and experience levels Every ticket purchased helps Dancing In The Streets AZ provide scholarships, bring professional guest artists to Tucson, and make ballet accessible through our "Ballet for Everybody" mission. Thank you for supporting the arts and changing lives through dance. www.ditsaz.org
